Los Angeles, California · eat

Restaurants in Los Angeles for cyclists

Where to eat in Los Angeles the night before and the afternoon after. Real food, open when you need it.

Restaurants in Los Angeles for cyclists, listed

  1. Reddi Chick BBQ

    • Barbecue
    • 225 26th Street #23, Santa Monica, CA 90402
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Reddi Chick BBQ

    After the ride, on the Westside: a counter in the Brentwood Country Mart, the corner where Velo Club La Grange’s weekday rides (Tue, Wed, Thu and Fri, 6:30 am) leave. Open 10 to 7 every day, so lunch, not breakfast. Barbecue chicken, ribs and baked potatoes, per its site. Seating and bike parking were not on the page.

  2. Pine & Crane Silverlake

    The night before, on the east side: noodle soup and rice plates at a counter in Silver Lake, at the Sunset Triangle, on the Griffith Park side of town.

    • Taiwanese
    • 1521 Griffith Park Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90026
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Pine & Crane Silverlake

    Noon to 10, closed Tuesday. No reservations; a group lines up. Some seating outside in the plaza next door, per its site.

  3. Canter’s Deli

    Late, and early: 6 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. Monday to Friday, from 5 a.m. Sunday, all night Saturday, per its site.

    • Deli
    • 419 N Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90036
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Canter’s Deli

    A big room on Fairfax between the Westside and the east side. Takes a group at any hour. Breakfast all day.

  4. Brent’s Deli Northridge

    • Deli
    • 19565 Parthenia Street, Northridge, CA 91324
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Brent’s Deli Northridge

    After the ride, in the Valley: the Northridge deli in the same neighborhood as the CSUN lot where SFVBC’s club ride (Saturdays and Sundays, 8:00 am) leaves. Opens at 8 every day; closes at 8, or 3 on Monday. Outdoor tables and bike parking were not on its page.

  5. Martha’s 22nd Street Grill

    • Breakfast
    • 25 22nd St, Hermosa Beach, CA 90254
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Martha’s 22nd Street Grill

    After the ride, South Bay: breakfast and lunch on a patio in Hermosa Beach with the sand in view, on the beach path and north of the Redondo Beach start of the Donut Ride (Saturdays, 8:00 am). 7 to 3 every day, per OpenTable and a listing with 2026 reviews. No site of its own; (310) 376-7786.

  6. The Rock Store

    On the way, in the mountains: the motorcycle roadhouse on Mulholland Highway, the road the Latigo loop jogs onto at Kanan.

    • Diner
    • 30354 Mulholland Highway, Cornell, CA 91301
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about The Rock Store

    Breakfast and lunch on an outside patio, weekends only: 7 to 6 Saturday and Sunday, 9 to 6 Friday, closed Monday to Thursday, per TripAdvisor and a September 2025 local guide. Call (818) 889-1311 before you count on it.

  7. The Donut Man

    On the way, in the foothills: the donut shop on Route 66 in Glendora, the town at the bottom of Glendora Mountain Road.

    • Donuts
    • 915 E Route 66, Glendora, CA 91740
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about The Donut Man

    Before or after GMR and the Baldy loop. Open 24 hours every day, per its site; (626) 335-9111.
